subject: Inference acceptance & loadbook: hosting variants verification
messages:
From: Carlos Ruiz <c.ruiz@starlite.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-21 09:12 PDT
Subject: Inference acceptance criteria + initial load profile

Hi Hannah / Karthik,

Thanks for taking this on. Attached is our representative load profile and a short note on our acceptance goals. High level:
- Peak concurrent sessions: 500 sustained for 30m windows
- Steady-state concurrency: ~200 with occasional spikes to 700 for short bursts
- Latency targets: P95 generation latency target ~120ms (token-level), TTFT for end-to-end chat responses median < 1.2s
- Throughput: target sustained token/sec across the fleet; we'll share sample transcripts to estimate tokenization variance

We're working on procurement and need the MAP and the acceptance matrix to feed into our SOW and procurement schedule (targeting sign-off by 2027-08-31). Can Redwood run the same suite across hosted / dedicated / private so we can compare isolation, autoscaling behavior, and predictability?

Attachments: starlite-workload-summary.json (stl profile)

Thanks,
Carlos
VP Infra, Starlite AI
ops@starlite.ai
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>
To: Carlos Ruiz <c.ruiz@starlite.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-21 11:03 PDT
Subject: Re: Inference acceptance criteria + initial load profile

Carlos — appreciate the clarity. We can definitely run the three-mode comparison and bake results into the MAP. Quick outline of what I'll run with the team:

1) Acceptance matrix (attached): we will populate thresholds for latency (p50/p95/p99), TTFT, steady throughput, and failure rate per model variant.
2) Run sequence: Hosted -> Dedicated (reserved pool) -> Private (customer VPC image) to minimize risk and provide progressive isolation checks.
3) Tests to run per mode:
   - Ramp and soak (steps to 200, 350, 500 concurrent sessions), 30m soak windows
   - Burst test (simulate 700 concurrent short spikes 5x)
   - KV cache warm vs cold runs to measure TTFT improvements
   - Autoscaling exercise (configure Dedicated autoscale policy to our standard policy; for Private we run with node counts you provide)
4) Observability: we'll capture token-level latency histograms, concurrency traces, full error logs, and cost delta estimates per run.

I attached the Redwood acceptance matrix template and a blank MAP doc link — if you can confirm the procurement timeline and give a remote access token (read-only) for telemetry ingestion, we'll schedule the first hosted run for 2027-08-23 morning (PST).

Attachments: redwood-acceptance-matrix.xlsx, loadbook-v2.xlsx
Related link: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1XMAPStarlite-MAP

If that timeline works, I'll loop in Marcus and Neha to own orchestration and billing checks.

—Hannah
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
hannah@redwood.ai
From: Carlos Ruiz <c.ruiz@starlite.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-22 08:45 PDT
Subject: Re: Inference acceptance criteria + initial load profile

Thanks Hannah — schedule works. A couple of clarifications before you run:
- For Private tests we will provide a 3-node cluster image (Ubuntu + our network overlay) — I'll drop the image link into the MAP doc.
- Can you run a targeted autoscale noise test for Dedicated: 1) scale-to-zero behavior when burst drops to 0, 2) scale-up latency from idle-to-500 conc. We want data on how quickly Dedicated returns to steady throughput under load.
- For telemetry: we can provide a read-only API key for ingest; I'll attach an updated workload sample that includes token distribution.

Attachments: starlite-workload-summary.json (v2)

Also, procurement is asking if Redwood can provide a short summary of predictability differences (single-paragraph) to drop into our SOW. If you can provide that with numbers from the runs that would be ideal.

Carlos
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-22 13:17 PDT
Subject: Internal: orchestration plan for Starlite acceptance runs

Karthik / Marcus / Neha — internal notes and who-owns-what for the Starlite MAP runs: 

- Hosted run (Hannah/Karthik): 2027-08-23 09:00 PST\  * Goal: baseline latency + TTFT with no reservation constraints. Watch for burst-induced queueing on our shared pool.
- Dedicated run (Marcus): 2027-08-23 16:00 PST\  * Use reserved pool with standard autoscaling policy: min replicas 2, scale step 2, cooldown 45s. Run the scale-to-zero noise test Carlos requested by dropping traffic to zero for 20m and then firing a 700 conc spike.
- Private run (Neha): 2027-08-24 09:00 PST\  * Starlite will provide 3-node image. We'll deploy the VPC connector and run the same loadbook. Pay attention to network variance — this is expected.

Acceptance thresholds I put in the matrix draft: p95 gen latency <= 120ms, median TTFT <= 1.3s, error rate < 0.5%. If we see cold-KV TTFT > 2.5s we'll note caching impact and recommend pre-warm.

Immediate asks: Marcus — prepare Dedicated pool and quota. Neha — prep Private deployment checklist and KMS handshake. Karthik — I'll need the load generator config and the Grafana dashboard link to snapshot after each run.

Notes from last quick test (hosted warm run): median TTFT ~1.25s but P95 spiked to ~240ms during a 90s burst — likely due to transient queueing. We'll capture traces and correlate to batch sizing.

—Hannah
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Carlos Ruiz <c.ruiz@starlite.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-23 11:30 PDT
Subject: Re: Inference acceptance criteria + initial load profile — run results and summary

Carlos / Hannah — attaching the consolidated results from the three runs. TL;DR bullets first:
- Hosted (baseline): steady 200 conc OK. P95 token latency: 110–260ms (260ms observed only during 700 conc bursts); TTFT median 1.22s. Cost baseline: lowest per-token but variance during bursts.
- Dedicated (reserved pool): much tighter P95 window 115–140ms even at 500 conc; scale-from-idle to 500 conc measured ~38s in our run (with our autoscale policy). Scale-to-zero noise test showed a 30–45s transient recovery.
- Private (customer VPC): median latency similar to Dedicated when network stable; observed extra jitter (~20–60ms) attributable to egress NAT and overlay. TTFT comparable when KV warmed.

Attachments: results-aggregated.csv, grafana_snapshot.png
Related link: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/starlite-loadbook/dashboard?orgId=1

Next steps proposed for MAP & SOW:
1) We'll populate the acceptance matrix with observed numbers (I pushed a draft to the MAP doc).
2) For procurement language: one-paragraph summary attached below.
3) Schedule a brief sign-off call on 2027-08-25 to finalize SOW and Dedicated sizing.

Quoted summary for SOW (pasteable):
"Redwood ran an identical loadbook across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. Dedicated infrastructure provided the most predictable P95 latency and fastest cold-to-peak scale; Hosted offered the lowest average unit cost but exhibited transient P95 spikes under extreme bursts; Private deployments matched Dedicated performance when network topology was stable, with occasional jitter attributable to customer network conditions."

—Karthik
From: Carlos Ruiz <c.ruiz@starlite.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>
Cc: Angela Park <angela.park@growthpartners.com>
Date: 2027-08-24 17:05 PDT
Subject: Re: Inference acceptance criteria + initial load profile — run results and summary

Thanks team — that summary is exactly what procurement wanted. We're good to move to SOW drafting. Please add the finalized acceptance matrix to the MAP doc and I'll route for internal sign-off.

Next steps:
- Hannah: finalize MAP and attach the acceptance matrix in the doc by 2027-08-25 EOD PST.
- Marcus: provide Dedicated capacity sizing estimate and monthly commitment options for the SOW.
- Redwood to share final Grafana snapshots and the per-run CSVs in the MAP folder.

I'll plan the sign-off call for 2027-08-25 09:00 PST — Angela from Growth Partners will join to assist with procurement.

Carlos
VP Infra, Starlite AI
